_comment: Absolute oral bioavailability measured at more than one dose — the empirical F-vs-dose line for a drug whose intestinal absorption saturates, and the flat line of the drug it is taught against. Doses are stated on the basis the source reports them (`doseBasis`); converting a divided daily dose to a single dose means assuming a dosing frequency, which is a modeling step and stays in code.

_doseBasis.per_day: Total daily dose, divided across the day as the label directs.

series.citationText: FDA NEURONTIN label (NDA 020235); Gidal et al. 1998 (PMID 9714500)
series.notes: Saturable: intestinal uptake rides the system-L / LAT1 amino-acid carrier, so the absorbed fraction falls as the dose climbs and total exposure flattens out. Divided three times daily on the label regimen these points came from.

Dose-linear: the same α2δ-1 drug uses the carrier in a non-saturating regime and stays ≥ ~90% absorbed at any dose. The five points span the starting-to-maximum therapeutic range (75–600 mg/day); the same value would hold outside it, so this is a flat line rather than a measured decline.
